newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Italian options volatilities see-saw.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Italian options volatilities see-saw.

text.p: Volatility of Italian debt options traded on LIFFE flicked higher on Monday in the wake of Friday's sell off, before sliding back later in the session as futures stabilised, traders said.
The end of the previous week's trading saw Italian BTPs plunge amid concerns that European Economic and Monetary Union could be delayed from its proposed start date of January 1999.
Volatility closed towards 8.6 percent on Friday, was quoted as high as 8.85 percent for at-the-money straddles early on Monday, and shuddered down to 8.0-8.5 percent by 1500 GMT.
"You'd be a brave man to sell it cheaper," said a broker at a major British brokerage in London. "It's a very choppy market and the delay talk is still in the market."
September volatility rose to 8.4 percent from just below 8.0 percent on Friday.
June BTP futures were up one basis point at 127.51.
Traders said there were relatively few directional trades going through, as investors were unwilling to put on new strategies until the dust from last week had settled.
"The spreads are very wide, and the market is still edgy," said a trader at an Italian bank in Milan. "People are still finding volatility attractive as a buy."
However, he said the major downmove in BTP futures was over, and the market was expected to stabilise in the short term.
At the short end, June Eurolira options volatility also ticked up towards 19.0 percent early on, but fell back later on to the 18.7-19.7 percent level.

The most notable trade was a 93.75 middle call butterfly, which was popular throughout the session. LIFFE data show that more than 13,000 calls were traded at the 93.75 strike, more than 15,000 at 94.00 and more than 12,500 at 93.50.
June Eurolira futures were up one basis point at 93.02.
